finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id: the boolean result of authorized() is discarded, so any authenticated user can delete any project regardless of ownership. The sibling PUT route correctly uses authorize(), which throws.
finding.source: Authenticated low-privilege user sends DELETE /projects/:id with another user's project id (req.params.id)

trace.note: DELETE route entry, id from req.params
project loaded by id with no ownership scoping
authorized() returns boolean; return value ignored, no throw or return
authorized() only returns true/false and never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() result unused (api.js:18). No other middleware is visible in this repo; req.user and req.store are assumed to come from upstream code not in this directory. Compared with PUT at api.js:25, which uses the throwing authorize() and is safe.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: authorized() at api.js:18 is a bare statement whose boolean result (api.js:12-14) is discarded; no middleware in this directory
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() (api.js:12-14) and ignores the result, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, unlike the throwing authorize() used at api.js:25.
